Distort

/dis-TORT/ — rhymes with court · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To distort something is to twist or change its natural shape or appearance so it looks different from reality.

The funhouse mirrors distort your reflection into wavy shapes.

Worked Example

The photographer used filters to distort the landscape, stretching the mountains into impossible shapes and colors.

Distort captures the idea of deliberately twisting something into a false or unreal appearance. A plain word like 'changed' doesn't convey the idea of bending it into something unrecognizable.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

twist: to bend something out of its shape

warp: to bend gradually out of true form

alter: to change something from its original state

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

clarify: to make something clear and accurate

straighten: to return something to its true shape

Where it sits · how badly the real shape is lost — change → twist → warp → distort

change vs. distort: Change is far weaker than distort; change simply means making something different, while distort means twisting it until it misrepresents reality.

twist vs. distort: Twist is weaker than distort: a twist bends something partway, but to distort is to twist it so thoroughly that its true form disappears.

warp vs. distort: Warp is slightly weaker than distort — warping bends something out of true, while distorting deforms it so completely that it gives a false picture.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart; completely (Latin)

Root — tort

Root — tort: to twist (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Dis- means 'apart' or 'completely' and the Latin root tort means 'to twist,' so distort literally means 'to twist different ways' — twisting something so far out of its true shape or meaning that it no longer matches reality.

Use the root in a new word: contortionist

Use the root in a new word: contortionist: The contortionist twisted her body into impossible knots, showing off the same Latin root tort, 'to twist,' that gives distort its meaning.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Use distort when something is deliberately or noticeably twisted into a false or unreal appearance. For simple changes or modifications, 'change' or 'modify' is simpler and often better.
